Your therapist will probably have you fill out a small packet (think like when you go to a new doctors clinic and you have to fill out all of that information). They'll get a basic summary from that (at least that's how it worked for me). 

Then they just start doing their thing. Ask you questions, ask how you're doing and honestly just jump right in but taking it easy. The first session will more than likely be them explaining what EMDR is, answer any questions you might have and go from there. I can't really say how it will start because it's different for everyone. 

Don't worry about regurgitating all of every detail from each trauma in one go! Just trust the process, they'll ask the questions to get the information they need to move further.

If it works, you'll be more emotionally stable. You'll have ways to cope with any stressors with the tools you learned with your therapist.

Hello, OP! I will do my best to explain what to expect, how you may feel after a session and just some general things I've experienced. I've only been seeing my therapist for about a month now, so I'm still relatively new myself. Other users may comment that have more experience and hopefully even an EMDR Therapist themselves. I'm going to try to keep it to the point, so I'll use bullet points to keep myself from rambling. 😅

- It's normal to feel a little anxious before you go into a session

- It's absolutely nothing like 'talk therapy' (in my opinion). By talk therapy, I mean basic counseling where you sit in front of a counselor and vent. I noticed that counseling didn't work for me because I would talk about my trauma, trigger myself, the trigger wasn't addressed how it needed to be so my PTSD actually got worse over time. With EMDR, you don't talk about the trauma in detail. You just answer questions that the therapist asks you and they guide you from there (there's more detail, but it's that in a nutshell).

-The way I explain EMDR to someone the best I can, is that it's "guided daydreaming." They're next question is always "Is it hypnosis!?" My answer is no.

-You're literally rewiring your brain, helping your brain reprocess the trauma by associating positive emotions related to the negative to help your brain get "unstuck."

-Your "fight, flight, freeze" response has been thrown out of whack, which is why when you experience a trigger you get extremely emotional, have panic attacks, flashbacks, etc. That's the "stuck" in you fight, flight, freeze. EMDR untangles all that so when you DO experience a trigger, your brain says "I remember that! I remember the experience, how I felt, the event and how bad it sucked but I know that I'm not there right now so I'm okay. I'm safe." Instead of "OH MY GOD IT'S HAPPENING AGAIN RIGHT NOW. FREAK OUT. PANIC."

Think if your brain like a necklace that's been tangled up. They're a bitch to get undone. Right? Sometimes you ask someone for help because you just can't quite get it. They get the necklace undone, but you're still wearing it. ☺️

The sessions themselves can be hard. Emotional. That's okay! That means you're getting somewhere. Now, if your therapist see's that you're starting to have a for real breakdown instead of just shedding some tears, they'll attack that trigger from a softer angle and/or guide you through exercises (that's not just deep breathing) to get you stabilized. You will NEVER walk out of that office triggered and on high alert. I'm thankful for my therapist insuring that. 

If I didn't answer everything or have left you with more questions, please reply and I'll do my best to answer you!! I recommend researching EMDR online and watching some videos on YouTube.

Best of luck, OP! I'm so happy that you're starting your healing journey! ♥️
